SCALE MEASURED 2026-07-24: 1,143 Central Oregon subdivisions have >=10 lifetime SFR sales (1,662 total CO subs) — x4 period types = ~4,572 RPC calls, each a full-table scan (~seconds) = HOURS of compute. The compute RPC public.compute_and_cache_period_stats (supabase/migrations/20260425090000) ALREADY accepts geo_type=subdivision, but (1) it scopes a subdivision by lower("SubdivisionName")=lower(p_geo_slug) — NAME-ONLY, no city qualifier — so same-named subdivisions across cities COLLIDE/merge (a §0 data-accuracy disaster); (2) READ-KEY CORRECTED 2026-07-24 (the prior note here was WRONG — do not trust the composite claim): the /subdivisions/[slug] page passes its RAW route slug to getMarketStats({geoType:'subdivision', geoSlug: slug}) (page.tsx:363), NOT a composite bend:tetherow. For a registry subdivision the route slug is slugify(alias) (e.g. 'tetherow', resolved via resolveRegistryAlias matching slugify(alias)===slug against data/resort-communities.json). The boundaries.geo_slug values (what getIndexableSubdivisions derives from) are slugified VERBOSE PLAT names — e.g. 'broken-top-phase-i-a-replat-lots-47-thru-51', 'arrowwood-trail-broken-top-phase-iv-f' — only 113 subdivision-boundary rows total, NOT clean names. So the slug scheme is INCONSISTENT across three systems: registry aliases (clean single-token), boundaries (verbose plat slugs), and listings.SubdivisionName (mixed clean/verbose). BEFORE writing ANY subdivision stat the next pass MUST decide the aggregation unit + the matching write-key: per-plat (113 boundary slugs) is too SPARSE to clear a stats threshold; the meaningful unit is the CLEAN registry name (e.g. Broken Top = all its plats), whose read-key is slugify(alias). Mechanism to add: the cron in vercel.json + a test/gate asserting geo_type=subdivision rows exist for qualifying subs.
